nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a compact topological group and let $\rho$ be a representation of $G$ on a finite-dimensional real normed space $V$ such that the action map $G \times V \to V$, $(g, v) \mapsto \rho(g)(v)$, is continuous. Then $\rho$ is semisimple: every subrepresentation of $\rho$ has a complementary subrepresentation.
nodes.title: Representations of compact groups are semisimple

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a compact Hausdorff topological group and let $x \ne y$ be elements of $G$. Then there are an integer $n > 0$ and a continuous map $\rho$ from $G$ to the complex $n \times n$ matrices such that $\rho(1) = 1$, $\rho(gh) = \rho(g)\rho(h)$ for all $g, h \in G$, the matrix $\rho(g)$ is unitary for every $g \in G$, and $\rho(x) \ne \rho(y)$.
nodes.title: Peter–Weyl theorem: unitary representations separate points
